Hi Olivia
- great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps to validate embeddings for Acme's product search use case:

1) Goals we heard: improve semantic recall for product search (+faceted matching), reduce stale results from catalog drift, and keep vector index at ~2-3M vectors with sub-100ms nearest-neighbor latency.

2) Immediate asks from our side: a small sample of the product catalog (CSV with id, title, description, category), and a few representative queries (search logs or sample queries).

3) Recommended evaluation plan (high level):
   - Run embed + offline retrieval bench (Recall@10, MRR, median rank, avg cosine distance) on sample set
   - Compare 2 model families: redwood-embed-1024-v2 (higher-dim dense, tested on retail) and open-embed-768-quant (lower-dim but cheaper)
   - Check drift sensitivity by simulating recent vs. historical subsets and measuring distribution shift (cosine shift, norm changes)

Links: I'll share a short benchmark template and prompt set after you drop the sample.

Proposed timeline: we can get a first-pass bench within 48-72 hours after you share the sample. After that we'll propose next steps for pilot and production config (index dims, PQ settings, refresh cadence).

Thanks - Marcus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Embeddings fit validation follow-up: recommended models + next steps

Hi Olivia - thanks for the sample, that's very helpful. Initial read & recommendations below after skimming the sample: 

Short answers: yes, go higher-dim for initial evaluation. We recommend testing: 
- redwood-embed-1024-v2 (1024-d) - better capture of longer descriptions / nuance
- open-embed-768-quant (768-d) - cheaper, faster ops; good baseline

Planned bench metrics: Recall@1, Recall@5, Recall@10, MRR, median rank, average cosine similarity for positives vs. random negatives, and drift delta (change in mean similarity between older vs. newer SKUs). We'll also compute index size and approximate query latency at 2M vectors (simulate with PQ/residual quant).

Attachments: I’m attaching the benchmark CSV we’ll use to record results and our prompt_set_v2.txt (the prompt_set includes synthetic user query paraphrases and negative mining heuristics).

Pilot plan (48-72h after sample received):
- Day 1: preprocess & create eval splits (historical vs. recent) + generate embeddings for both models
- Day 2: run retrieval bench + produce condensed report and recommended index dims/PQ settings
- Day 3: quick follow-up call to review results, propose pilot/rollout plans, and discuss auto-refresh cadence (daily delta vs. streaming)

Quality/regression concerns: if we see meaningful regression on recent SKUs with the cheaper model, we recommend keeping redwood-embed-1024-v2 for the production index and using open-embed for a cold-cache tier. Rollback path: index snapshot + versioned index metadata (we’ll keep both).

I’ll kick off the bench once Marcus confirms compute & scheduling.

Best - Marissa
